reasoning_steps: Extensive scientific research and double-blind, placebo-controlled studies have failed to establish a causal link between monosodium glutamate (MSG) and the cluster of symptoms historically dubbed "Chinese restaurant syndrome" (such as headaches, numbness, and flushing)
The concept originated from an anecdotal letter published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1968 rather than rigorous clinical trials
Major food safety and health organizations, including the U.S

Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the World Health Organization (WHO), classify MSG as "generally recognized as safe" (GRAS), noting that the human body metabolizes added glutamate identically to naturally occurring glutamate found in foods like tomatoes and parmesan cheese

While a tiny subset of individuals may have mild, transient sensitivity to unusually large doses consumed without food, there is no consistent evidence that typical dietary MSG consumption causes these symptoms.

claim_traces.claim_title: Social media causes depression in teenagers
claim_traces.claim_text: "Social media use causes depression and anxiety in teenagers."
reasoning_steps: Whether social media use directly *causes* depression and anxiety in adolescents is a subject of significant scientific debate
While numerous studies, public health advisories (such as the U.S

Surgeon General's Advisory), and organizations like the Mayo Clinic and Child Mind Institute document strong correlations and elevated risks of depressive and anxiety symptoms among heavy users, establishing a direct causal relationship remains controversial

Prominent researchers (such as Amy Orben and Andrew Przybylski) have found that the overall association across large datasets has very small effect sizes and that evidence for direct causation is weak, suggesting that reverse causality (teens who are already depressed or anxious turning to social media) or confounding variables (such as sleep disruption, cyberbullying, or pre-existing mental health issues) often explain the link
Conversely, other researchers (such as Jonathan Haidt and Jean Twenge) argue that experimental and longitudinal data demonstrate a causal role
Because the scientific community remains divided on causality versus correlation, the blanket claim of causation is disputed.

claim_traces.claim_title: Generative AI will replace 300 million jobs
claim_traces.claim_text: "Generative AI will replace 300 million jobs worldwide."
reasoning_steps: The claim overstates and mischaracterizes the findings of a widely cited March 2023 Goldman Sachs report

The report estimated that generative AI could expose the equivalent of approximately 300 million full-time jobs to automation globally, rather than definitively predicting that 300 million workers will be laid off or replaced
Crucially, the authors distinguished between tasks being automated and entire jobs being eliminated, noting that most occupations would be complemented rather than substituted by AI
Additionally, the study noted that technological disruption historically drives new job creation and estimated a significant boost to global GDP over time
Framing this projection as a definitive forecast that AI "will replace 300 million jobs" ignores these essential economic nuances.

claim_traces.claim_title: US Congress passed no budget on time since 1997
claim_traces.claim_text: "The US Congress has not passed a complete federal budget on time since 1997."
reasoning_steps: Under the modern congressional budget process established by the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 (which took effect for fiscal year 1977), Congress is required to pass all regular appropriations bills before the start of the fiscal year on October 1

According to analyses from the Pew Research Center, Congressional Research Service, and government data, Congress has enacted all of its regular annual spending bills on time in only four fiscal years: 1977, 1989, 1995, and 1997

Since fiscal year 1997, Congress has consistently relied on continuing resolutions (stopgap funding) or late omnibus spending packages rather than enacting all individual appropriations bills before the statutory deadline.

search_results.title: Congress hasn’t passed a budget on time since 1997. We should fix that.
search_results.snippet: December 18, 2025 - The Constitution grants Congress the “power of the purse” through Article I, Section 9, which states that “No Money shall be drawn from the Treasury, but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law.” Critically, the Constitution doesn’t mandate the current authorization and annual appropriations process currently used. It simply requires that spending be authorized by law. The “textbook” legislative process requires Congress to pass approximately 12 appropriations bills by Oct. 1 for the following fiscal year — something Congress hasn’t done since 1996. Instead, the country lurches from continuing resolution to continuing resolution, with shutdowns or their threat becoming routine weapons in partisan warfare. Federal agencies can’t plan, contractors face uncertainty, and essential services hang in the balance while politicians posture.

claim_traces.claim_title: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood
claim_traces.claim_text: "Octopuses have three hearts and their blood is blue."
reasoning_steps: The claim is biologically accurate
Octopuses have three hearts: two branchial hearts that pump blood through the gills and one systemic heart that circulates oxygenated blood through the rest of the body
Additionally, their blood is blue because it uses a copper-rich protein called hemocyanin (rather than iron-based hemoglobin) to transport oxygen, which appears blue when oxygenated.
